howDoI.q: How do I put a shadow under a character?
How do I make a shadow that lets the ground show through?
How do I use one map with two sets of pictures?
How do I make a shadow that shrinks when something hops?
How do I make a monster hover above its own shadow?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Little Shadows is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about shadows under characters and monsters: a flat shadow on the ground, a checkerboard one that lets the ground show through, a shadow that shrinks when something hops, and a bee that hovers over a shadow of its own. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

A game here has no see-through colors, so a shadow cannot darken the ground. It is only more pixels, painted into the picture of whatever casts it. Everything in this game is a trick for making those pixels look right.

The keys

The Left and Right arrows walk Mara, and Space jumps. Walk into a door to go through it. Nothing in this game hurts Mara, and the critters walk straight through her.

pages.head: Level 1: The Yard
pages.html:
Level 1: The Yard

A stone wall at the back and a long strip of ground in front of it: sand, then grass, then dark soil. A friendly pip waddles on each. You play the yard twice. The first time every shadow is solid: one dark color, the same on every ground. The second time it is dithered: a checkerboard of that color and nothing, so the ground shows through the gaps.

Walk along and look at Mara's feet and at the pips. On sand and grass the solid shadow is strong and the dithered one is soft. On the dark soil the dithered one almost disappears and the solid one is still there, which is the trade: a dithered shadow is lighter on any ground, and a solid one is stronger on any ground.

The second door leads on to the hop.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the yard is made

  • The shadow is part of the picture. Mara's standing and walking pictures in solid.cbl have a flat oval painted behind her feet, in the bottom rows of the block. The same oval is painted behind each pip in solid.mbl. Nothing else in the game knows the shadow is there.
  • Dithering. In dither.cbl and dither.mbl the same oval is painted on every other pixel (a checkerboard). The others stay color 255, which is clear, so whatever is under the sprite shows through. That is why it is lighter on every ground.
  • Room under the feet. Mara's feet used to touch the bottom of her block. Her body is three pixels shorter here (three rows of her shirt come out), so there is room for the shadow under her shoes.
  • The ground. The strip Mara stands in is a row of ordinary blocks (lane.sand, lane.grass, lane.soil) that the hero can walk through, drawn with the ground's color right down to the bottom of the block, with solid blocks in the same color under it. That is what lets a shadow sit on the ground and not on the sky.
  • One map, two scenes. Scene 2 and scene 3 both list yard.map. They differ in the three files that hold pictures: solid.bbl or dither.bbl (the signs), solid.mbl or dither.mbl (the pips) and solid.cbl or dither.cbl (Mara). See Same House, Many Rooms for more on one map in several scenes.

Shadow pixels are drawn in purple here so you can see where they are. In the game they are the dark ink color.

pages.head: Level 2: The Hop
pages.html:
Level 2: The Hop

The same courtyard, all grass. Three pips hop on the spot, side by side. The first has no shadow and looks as if it floats. The second has a shadow that never changes, and looks stuck to the ground under it with nothing to say how high it is. The third has a dithered shadow that gets small at the top of the hop and big again as it lands, which is how a shadow behaves when something goes up.

Walk past them and jump over one yourself. Mara's own shadow is painted into her standing and walking pictures, so it goes while she is in the air.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the hop is made

  • A hop is six pictures. hopShrink.0 to hopShrink.5 are the pip a little higher in each, to the top and back, with the squashed one first (it has just landed). Each is shown for its own time, longest on the ground, so it spends a beat on the grass and then goes up and down quickly.
  • The body moves; the shadow stays on the ground. The shadow is painted in the same rows of the block in every picture. Only the body moves up the block, so the shadow is left behind, on the ground, as it should be.
  • The shadow shrinks. Its width is 16 pixels on the ground and about 7 at the top, in six steps. A dither keeps the soft look through every size.
  • Two ways to get it wrong. hopNone is the same body with no shadow. hopSame keeps one solid shadow, 14 pixels wide, in all six pictures.
  • No path. The monsters stand still: the hop is the animation only. The pictures play in order and loop (a monster's pic list in the Monsters tab).

pages.head: Level 3: The Hover
pages.html:
Level 3: The Hover

A bee flies over the sand. The first bee is two blocks tall: the bee is a monster, and its shadow is a second monster in the block right below. The bottom block is nothing but the shadow. The second bee is three blocks up, with two empty blocks between it and its shadow, and looks higher for it.

Both bees bob a little and fly back and forth. Their shadows go with them, and get a little bigger as the bee comes down.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How the hover is made

  • Two monsters. A monster is one block, so a bee that is two blocks tall is a bee (monster 4) and a shadow (monster 5) placed one above the other in hover.map. The shadow is a block with nothing in it but the dithered oval.
  • The same path and the same speed. Both have the same path (out four blocks and back, speed 1) and start together, so they never come apart. The Monsters tab shows each one's path.
  • The same loop of four pictures, each shown for 3 ticks: the bee bobs down two and four pixels and back up, wings up and down, while its shadow gets wider and narrower to match. Nearer the ground is wider.
  • Height is a gap. The low bee's block is right above its shadow's. The high bee's block is three up. The gap is the height; the shadow is the same.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot darken the ground. A picture's pixels replace what is under them, or they are clear. There is no see-through color, so a solid shadow is the same dark color on sand and on soil, and a dithered one only leaves half the pixels clear.
  • A dither can shimmer. The checkerboard belongs to the sprite and the ground does not move with it, so over a ground with its own fine pattern the two can fight as the sprite walks. A plain ground is kinder to it.
  • A shadow painted into a picture goes where the picture goes. That is why the hop moves the body inside its block and leaves the shadow in place. A picture that jumps up a block would take its shadow with it, which is why Mara's own shadow is only in her standing and walking pictures. A shadow that has to stay behind on the ground while its thing flies is a monster of its own, as the bee's is.
  • A monster is one block. A thing two blocks tall is two monsters. They stay together only because they have the same path and the same speed and start at the same time. A monster that dies, or is pulled by a chase, leaves its shadow behind.
  • Nothing here is cast by a light. The shadows are flat ovals directly under things. They do not stretch away from a sun or sit at different angles.
  • The picture is flat. Mara stands in the bottom of a block and the wall behind her is just drawn behind. There is no depth, so a shadow also has to look right there.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In dither.mbl, redraw pip0's shadow with every third pixel clear in place of every second and see how much lighter it looks.
  • In dither.mbl, change the Time of hopShrink.0 from 8 to 2 for a pip that hardly stops on the ground.
  • Make the shadow in hopShrink.3 (the top of the hop) as wide as the one on the ground and see how the hop feels wrong.
  • In the Monsters tab, give the shadow monster a different speed from the bee's and watch them come apart.
  • Draw a shadow for a monster that walks, and for one that flies low over water (use only a few clear pixels).
